subject: Model shortlist & token footprint — Nova Retail onboarding
messages:
From: Karen Li <karen.li@novaretail.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: impl-team@novaretail.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps for onboarding — model & volume questions

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before our kickoff next Tue, the engineering team asked us to get more concrete on the model options you recommend and an early token volume estimate so we can scope network and proxy capacity on our side. Key constraints:

- Primary workload is customer chat summarization + product taxonomy classification (post-chat).
- Typical chat length: 4–6 turns, average user message ~40 words.
- Peak concurrent sessions estimate: ~120 (we expect spikes during promo windows).
- Data residency: US-only; we will be on Redwood Dedicated.

Can you send a short recommended model shortlist (3–4 variants), guidance on context length we should provision, and a rough tokens/day estimate (conservative + expected) to feed into our infra plan? Also share any files you want us to review before the kickoff.

— Karen
Karen Li
Senior Product Manager, Nova Retail
karen.li@novaretail.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Li <karen.li@novaretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 12:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps for onboarding — model & volume questions

Hi Karen —

Thanks — this is helpful. High level answers below; I attached a compact matrix that maps capability, token cost, and context recommendations. See attachments: nova_model_shortlist_matrix.csv and nova_token_volume_estimates.xlsx

Shortlist (first-pass recommended):
- Redwood-Chat-13B (quantized) — Strong cost/perf for chats, good for summarization and short classification. Recommend if you want predictable latency at lower cost.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (fp16) — Small, fast, good for taxonomy classification; may need a separate classifier path for high-volume post-chat tasks.
- Llama2-70B-chat (8-bit) — Higher-quality summaries for long context and rare edge cases; use as fallback for long chats or canary.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (option) — Good middle ground for better instruction-following at moderate cost.

Context length guidance:
- Provision for 4k tokens as default (covers ~99% of your described chats).
- Offer a 16k-capable variant for sessions that include extended history, attachment transcripts, or agent notes — route those selectively.

Token volume back-of-envelope (conservative vs expected):
- Assume avg user input ~40 words (~60 tokens), 4 turns => ~240 user tokens/session.
- Model output for summarization ~200 tokens on average.
- End-to-end per session ~440 tokens.
- With 120 concurrent peak sessions and average 2 sessions/min churn during peak => peak throughput ~105,600 tokens/min (~6.3M tokens/hr).
- Daily: conservative (steady 25% peak for 10 hours + low usage off-peak) ~50M tokens/day; expected growth scenario ~120M tokens/day.

Operational notes & asks for the kickoff:
1) We'll present the shortlist and model-specific latency/throughput numbers for Dedicated pods.
2) Please confirm whether you need per-tenant encryption keys (KMS) so we can include Private config.
3) If you have a sample of 50 representative chats (anonymized), that will help us produce a tuned cost/quality recommendation.

I'll loop in Monica (onboarding) and Rishi (solutions) on the tactical plan. Proposed next step: 1-hour kickoff to align M.A.P. and finalize model pins.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Next steps for onboarding — model & volume questions

Adding the throughput/ops numbers Rishi style — quick summary for the matrix:

Assumptions (used to compute pod sizing):
- Avg tokens/session: 440 (Jonas baseline)
- Peak concurrent sessions: 120
- Request pattern: 60% single-turn requests (fast classification), 40% multi-turn generation (summarization)
- Latency SLO target: P95 < 600ms for chat path; P95 < 400ms for classification path

Recommended serving architecture:
- Two endpoint classes: 
  1) classification-fast: Mistral-Instruct-7B (1-2 A100s per pod, aggressive batching up to 64 tokens/window)
  2) chat-generation: Redwood-Chat-13B quantized (NVIDIA H100 / A100 mix depending on availability).
- Fallback pool: Llama2-70B (on-demand, can be lower QPS but used for high-quality or long-context sessions).

Pod sizing (baseline peak):
- Classification: 2 pods (each can handle ~1.2k classification reqs/min at target latency) => headroom for spikes.
- Chat-generation: 6 pods of 13B quantized workers (continuous batching + KV cache) to handle 6.3M tokens/hr peak with P95 ~480ms.
- Fallback 70B: 1 kept-warm instance for canary/edge cases; scale to 3 when long-context traffic >5% of total.

Token accounting notes:
- Enable prefix caching for returning sessions — expected to cut token spend for multi-turns by ~18-25% depending on repetition.
- Recommend rolling 1-week token retention for analytic features; we can advise retention and cost tradeoffs during onboarding.

Deliverables for kickoff: pod capacity numbers per model, expected monthly token burn, and an initial cost ballpark (we'll use the conservative token estimate to start). I'll drop a populated tab into the spreadsheet.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
